title: Sensitive browsing data disclosed

assumptions: Browsing data includes content that could be considered sensitive under privacy regulations

title: Users unaware of browsing data sharing with advertisers
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their browsing data is being shared with third-party advertisers, especially if this is a planned feature not yet disclosed.
assumptions: Users have not been explicitly informed about this data sharing practice

title: Lack of user control over browsing data sharing
description: Users may lack the ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their browsing data is shared with third-party advertisers.
assumptions: No opt-out or preference mechanism is in place for this data flow

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing browsing data with third-party advertisers may process more personal data than is actually needed for the recommendation engine's core functionality.
assumptions: The sharing with advertisers is not strictly necessary for the primary service function
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether advertiser sharing is considered necessary for the business model

title: Potential invalid consent for data sharing
description: Personal data collection and processing for sharing with advertisers may not rely on valid, informed consent from data subjects.
assumptions: Consent mechanisms may not adequately inform users about third-party advertiser sharing
uncertainty_note: Depends on current consent implementation

title: Processing of identified government ID data
description: Government ID images contain directly identified personal information (photos, names, ID numbers) that is being stored in the file system. This constitutes processing of identified data.
assumptions: Government ID images contain personally identifiable information

title: Unique identifiers in stored ID images
description: Government ID images contain unique identifiers (ID numbers, biometric data) that can directly reference the identity of data subjects.
assumptions: Government IDs contain unique identifying numbers or biometric data

title: Revealing attributes in ID images
description: Government ID images contain multiple revealing attributes (photo, name, address, date of birth, ID number) that support identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Government IDs contain multiple personal attributes

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: The unique identifiers in government ID images (ID numbers) can be used to link this data with other data stores or systems containing the same identifiers.
assumptions: ID numbers are used across multiple systems

title: Linking through quasi-identifiers
description: The combination of attributes in government ID images (name, DOB, address, photo) creates strong quasi-identifiers that can link data to individuals.
assumptions: Multiple attributes in ID images can be combined for identification

title: Highly sensitive data type stored
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data containing biometric and identifying information. Storing full images may exceed what is functionally required.
assumptions: Full ID images are stored rather than extracted data only

title: Data retention duration
description: Government ID images may be stored longer than functionally needed for authentication purposes, creating unnecessary privacy risk.
assumptions: Retention period is not clearly defined or limited
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about actual retention policy

title: Exposure to multiple parties
description: File system storage may expose government ID images to more parties than functionally necessary (e.g., system administrators, backup processes, other services).
assumptions: File system access controls may not be strictly limited
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about access control implementation

title: Unawareness of ID image storage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their government ID images are being collected and stored in the file system.
assumptions: Privacy notice may not clearly explain ID image storage
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about user notification practices

title: Lack of rectification/erasure control
description: Data subjects may lack control to request deletion or rectification of their stored government ID images.
assumptions: No clear mechanism for data subject rights requests
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about data subject rights implementation

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Storing full government ID images may violate GDPR data minimization if only specific data elements are needed for authentication.
assumptions: Full images stored rather than extracted data fields
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about functional requirements

title: Violation of storage limitation principle
description: Government ID images may be stored longer than necessary for the authentication purpose, violating storage limitation requirements.
assumptions: No clear retention policy or automatic deletion
uncertainty_note: Uncertain about retention policy

title: Attributable data evidence
description: Stored government ID images can be used as evidence to attribute actions or claims to specific individuals, potentially preventing deniability.
assumptions: ID images can be used as proof of identity for actions

title: Sensitive JWT data stored in localStorage
description: JWTs stored in browser localStorage may contain sensitive claims (user ID, roles, permissions, etc.) that are more sensitive than functionally required for session management. localStorage is accessible to any script on the same origin, creating exposure to XSS attacks.
assumptions: JWT contains user-identifying claims and is stored without additional protection

title: JWT accessible to dynamic set of parties via localStorage
description: localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript code running on the same origin, meaning the JWT could be accessed by malicious scripts or third-party libraries dynamically loaded on the page, exposing authentication tokens to unintended parties.
assumptions: Browser environment may load third-party scripts or be vulnerable to XSS

title: JWT retention in localStorage exceeds functional need
description: JWTs stored in localStorage persist until explicitly cleared by the application or user, potentially remaining longer than the authentication session requires, violating storage limitation principles.
assumptions: JWT is not automatically cleared on logout or session expiration

title: JWT contains unique identifier for data subject
description: JWTs typically contain user identifiers (sub claim, user ID, etc.) that uniquely reference the identity of the data subject, enabling identification when the token is accessed or intercepted.
assumptions: JWT contains standard claims including user identifier

title: JWT enables linking through unique identifier
description: The JWT stored in localStorage contains a unique identifier that can be used to link user activities across different sessions, pages, or even systems that accept the same JWT format.
assumptions: JWT contains persistent user identifier

title: User unaware of JWT storage in localStorage
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their authentication tokens are being stored in browser localStorage, nor understand the privacy implications of this storage mechanism.
assumptions: No explicit user notification about localStorage usage for authentication

title: Lack of user control over JWT erasure from localStorage
description: Users may lack direct control to rectify or erase JWTs stored in localStorage, depending on application implementation. This limits their ability to remove authentication data when no longer needed.
assumptions: No user-facing mechanism to clear localStorage authentication data

title: Potential violation of storage limitation principle
description: Storing JWTs in localStorage without automatic expiration or cleanup may violate GDPR storage limitation principle if tokens persist longer than necessary for the authentication purpose.
assumptions: JWT retention exceeds functional authentication session duration
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific JWT expiration and cleanup implementation

title: Sensitive child history data disclosed
description: Child history data is inherently sensitive personal information. The process P3 shares this data with the parent, which may include sensitive details about the child's activities, behaviors, or development that could be perceived as highly sensitive.
assumptions: Child history data contains sensitive personal information about the child

title: Excessive volume of child history data
description: The process may retrieve and share more child history data than is functionally needed for parent review, potentially including historical data beyond what is necessary for the current review purpose.
assumptions: The system retrieves full child history rather than filtered/limited data

title: Child identifier in shared data
description: The child history data likely contains unique identifiers (name, ID, etc.) that directly reference the child's identity, making the data identified rather than anonymized.
assumptions: Child history data includes direct identifiers

title: Revealing attributes in child history
description: Child history data contains revealing attributes (activities, behaviors, locations, etc.) that support identification of the child and could be used to distinguish them from others.
assumptions: Child history includes detailed behavioral or activity data

title: Quasi-identifier linking through child history
description: The combination of attributes in child history data (age, activities, school, etc.) could serve as quasi-identifiers that allow linking the data to the specific child.
assumptions: Child history contains multiple attributes that could combine to identify the child

title: Child unaware of data sharing with parent
description: The child (data subject) may not be aware that their history data is being shared with the parent for review, particularly if the child is young or if the system does not provide transparency about data flows.
assumptions: The child is not informed about data sharing with parent

title: Child lacks control over data sharing preferences
description: The child may lack the ability to set preferences or consent regarding how their history data is shared with the parent, especially if the child is a minor with limited legal capacity.
assumptions: Child has no mechanism to control or consent to data sharing

title: Insufficient data subject controls for child
description: The system may lack adequate support for the child's data subject rights (access, rectification, erasure, etc.) when their history is shared with the parent, potentially violating GDPR requirements for children's data.
assumptions: Child's data subject rights are not adequately supported in this flow

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Sharing child history data with the parent may process more personal data than is actually needed for the review purpose, potentially violating GDPR's data minimization principle.
assumptions: Full child history is shared rather than minimal necessary data

title: Child history data observable in transit
description: The child history data transmitted in this flow could be observed by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not properly secured, revealing sensitive information about the child.
assumptions: Data flow may not be encrypted or could be intercepted
